note: Literature confirms high penetrance (>75%) for core neurological signs like hypotonia and feeding difficulties in MSL2 syndrome, whereas organ anomalies occur 'to a lesser extent'.

evidence.text: In individuals with MSL2 variants, feeding difficulties occurred in 81.3% and hypotonia in 76.5%, supporting the hypothesis that core neurological and feeding signs exceed 60% penetrance.

source.title: MSL2 disruption leads to autism-like behaviors, impairs neurogenesis, and alters histone H4K16 acetylation
source.quote: were predominantly associated with feeding difficulties (81.3%) and hypotonia (76.5%).

evidence.text: The discovery study in a cohort of 25 individuals identifies hypotonia, motor coordination problems, and feeding difficulties as primary associations, while structural organ anomalies and seizures occur 'to a lesser extent'.

source.title: MSL2 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with lack of coordination, epilepsy, specific dysmorphisms, and a distinct episignature
source.quote: MSL2 variants were associated with NDD phenotypes including global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and motor issues such as coordination problems, feeding difficulties, and gait disturbance. Dysmorphisms and behavioral and/or psychiatric conditions, including autism spectrum disorder, and to a lesser extent, seizures, connective tissue disease signs, sleep disturbance, vision problems, and other organ anomalies, were observed in affected individuals.
